title: Order Matters: Competition-Guided Query Ordering for RNN-Based Object Detection

problem.summary: DETR-style detectors use one-to-one bipartite matching during training to assign object queries to ground-truth objects, enabling end-to-end set prediction without non-maximum suppression (NMS).
statements: DETR-style detectors use one-to-one bipartite matching during training to assign object queries to ground-truth objects, enabling end-to-end set prediction without non-maximum suppression (NMS).
However, without an explicit de-duplication procedure, multiple queries can still produce highly similar hypotheses for the same object, making training unstable and predictions less decisive.
Inspired by the sequential ordering of NMS, we propose DETRNN, a plug-and-play module that turns unordered object queries into a competition-aware sequence for recurrent refinement.

solution.summary: Transformer-based detectors such as DETR [1] unify object detection into an end-to-end set prediction problem.
solution.approach: Transformer-based detectors such as DETR [1] unify object detection into an end-to-end set prediction problem.
components: During training, DETR applies one-to-one bipartite matching between object queries and ground-truth objects, which removes post-processing NMS, avoiding manual threshold tuning.
Despite this elegant formulation, DETR still suffers from redundant hypotheses, especially in dense scenes (Fig. 1b).

Multiple queries can converge to similar regions with close confidence scores, but only one prediction can be matched to each ground-truth object, leaving the others as competing duplicates and slowing convergence.
